newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Four beaten to death in S.African street justice.
newsitem.headline: Four beaten to death in S.African street justice.

text.p: Four men were beaten to death after being "found guilty" of housebreaking by a kangaroo court in South Africa's KwaZulu-Natal province, police said on Monday.
The street justice meted out to the men occurred in the remote Qulashe area of the Zulu heartland.
"Four men were caught by the community for housebreaking. They were tried in a kangaroo court early on Sunday evening and then beaten to death," Captain Stephen Cloete told Reuters.
South Africans have become increasingly disillusioned with the way President Nelson Mandela's government is dealing with the country's escalating crime rate, which is one of the highest in the world.
A gang leader was beaten, burnt and shot to death in Cape Town in the southwest of the country last month by a vigilante Moslem group, People Against Gangsterism and Drugs (Pagad).
Police say the KwaZulu-Natal region on the east coast, which has 23,000 police members, needs another 8,000 officers to bring it up to acceptable standards for crime prevention.
